## Shared Notebook and Dashboard Project

[Download the project ZIP](files/research-project.zip){download="research-project.zip"}. Extract it and open its folder as an RStudio project. The bundle contains unchanged teaching data, shared validation/selection/plot functions, a complete Quarto notebook, a complete Shiny app and executable checks. Use its README from lesson 5 onwards; setup steps are in [Setup](setup.qmd).

Run `source("tests.R")` in the R console or `Rscript tests.R` in a terminal. Render `report.qmd`, change a recorded year and re-render, then run `shiny::runApp(".")`. Compare one observation across the input, notebook, app and download. Clear all country choices and inspect the message. A meaningful result needs both a successful run and source/interpretation checks.

**Keep:** the original inputs, notebook/app source, test results, a checked output and a brief note identifying parameters, assumptions and limitations. This public historical example has no upload facility and is not a template for sharing confidential data without an agreed arrangement.

## Practice: Explain a Gapminder Comparison

**Goal:** produce a short analysis that makes its data selection and limits visible. Work in the `applied_R` project prepared in setup, using `gapminder::gapminder`. These are historical country-level data, not measurements of individuals and not a current population dataset. Check the [package's data description](https://jennybc.github.io/gapminder/) before interpreting a result.

### 1. Inspect the Data

Use `head()`, `str()` and `names()` to inspect the table. Identify what one row represents and record the meaning and units of `year`, `lifeExp`, `pop` and `gdpPercap` from the data help page (`?gapminder::gapminder`). Check the available years rather than assuming that the table includes the present day.

**Check:** inspect uniqueness of the country–year combination. If that key is not unique in data you later substitute, investigate why before summarising or joining.

### 2. State and Implement a Question

Choose two countries that are present in the data and one recorded year. Filter to those country–year observations and select `country`, `year` and `lifeExp`. Retain the identifiers in the output.

**Check:** the filtered table should contain exactly the observations you intended. Compare its values with the corresponding original rows. An empty result is a reason to check spelling and available years, not to substitute a nearby observation silently.

### 3. Make a Figure with Context

Plot the available life-expectancy series for the two countries using ggplot2. Label the axes, name the countries and include the data source and historical coverage in a caption. Explain what changes over the recorded period without treating an association as evidence of a cause.

**Check:** inspect one plotted value against the filtered table. Make sure the plot covers the years you intended and that country identity remains clear without relying only on colour.

### 4. Save and Rerun

Save your analysis as an R script. Export the selected comparison table and figure into an `output` folder, separate from the input data. Record `sessionInfo()` with your working notes. Save the script, restart R and run it from the beginning with the project open.

**Keep:** the script, checked table, figure and a paragraph stating the question, selection, checks and limitations. Ask a partner to identify these in your work. If software access fails, annotate the lesson's example output with the selection and validation steps you would use.

### Debrief

Discuss: **What would change if the question concerned individuals rather than country-level averages?** The exercise supports a descriptive comparison at the level represented by the data. It does not justify claims about individual outcomes, a causal explanation or present-day conditions. Successful execution also does not validate an unexamined join or missing-value decision.

## A Script Handover Checklist

- Open the project and use paths relative to its folder.
- Put package loading and analysis parameters near the top of the script.
- Keep original data separate from derived tables and figures.
- Preserve row identifiers and record any filtering, missing-value or joining decisions.
- Check a small calculation manually and compare at least one output with its input.
- Save before restarting R, rerun from the beginning and retain `sessionInfo()` with the analysis record.

The [RStudio Projects guide](https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/ide/guide/code/projects.html) explains how projects organise working directories and files.

## Further Reading and Quick References

| Resource | Use it for |
|---|---|
| [An Introduction to R](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-intro.html) | Base R objects, indexing, functions and control flow |
| [R for Data Science, second edition](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/) | A structured follow-on route through importing, tidying, transforming and communicating data |
| [Introduction to dplyr](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/articles/dplyr.html) | Checking how filtering, selecting, grouping and summarising work |
| [ggplot2 documentation](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/) | Choosing geoms, labels, scales and plot structure |
| [Posit cheatsheets](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/) | A compact reminder after practising the corresponding lesson |
| [Gapminder package documentation](https://jennybc.github.io/gapminder/) | Understanding the source and coverage of the teaching data |
| [Quarto computations](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/computations/rstudio.html) | Keeping narrative, code and results in a reproducible document |
| [Shiny reactive flow](https://shiny.posit.co/r/getstarted/build-an-app/reactive-flow/reactive-flow.html) | Connecting controls and checked calculations to displayed outputs |

Consult documentation for your installed package version if syntax differs. A cheatsheet is a reminder; use the full help page to check arguments, types and missing-value behaviour.
